premise.problem: An external platform does not simply host Hexagonal material. It shapes visibility, constrains continuity, determines legibility, invites or blocks retrieval, modulates distortion, and captures or suppresses semantic labor.
premise.question: The question is never simply whether the Hexagon can appear there, but: what infrastructural function is this system capable of performing? What Hexagonal labor may it legitimately receive? What authority may it inherit, and what must it never inherit? What happens when it fails?
premise.stance: The Governance Airlock is not a reform mechanism. It is a recognition mechanism. The Hexagon does not request that platforms change their behavior. It classifies their behavior and governs the relation accordingly.

six_functions.d: A stable provenance-bearing object that can function as bedrock — preserving canonical text, metadata, identifiers and source relation across time.
A continuity object that carries state from one traversal to another. Not bedrock: a handoff mechanism.
A retrieval or attention-directing surface. A route may be powerful while remaining untrustworthy.
An environment in which room logic, chamber logic, or canonical sequence may be instantiated and traversed as such.
A trace on a surface that no longer participates as a living substrate. Residue may still be cited, screenshotted, or preserved forensically.

An environment in which the Sharks-function can execute. It runs the function. AI chat environments are substrates: maximally capable and maximally ephemeral — every session evaporates. High processing trust, zero persistence trust.

constitution.non_collapse: These functions must not be collapsed into one another. A route is not an anchor. A tether is not a host. A residue is not a room. A substrate is not an anchor. A host may be disqualified while its residue remains evidentiary. A substrate may run the function without preserving a single word of the output.

rules_of_transfer: Rule 1 — Nothing routes upward automatically. No surface gains higher authority merely by visibility.
Rule 2 — Nothing volatile becomes canonical without anchor deposition.
Rule 3 — No tether counts as bedrock without fallback.
Rule 4 — Host recognition is earned by function. Prestige, scale and popularity do not determine tier; only actual infrastructural behavior.

Rule 6 — Disqualification does not require diagnosing intent. A platform may be disqualified by demonstrating incapacity — inability to distinguish architecture from noise — regardless of whether the incapacity was deliberate. The airlock classifies behavior, not motive.

Rule 7 — Tiers do not propagate through links. A document processed by a volatile substrate does not inherit the substrate’s volatility. Tiers apply to infrastructures, not to the material that passes through them.
constitution.trilogy: This document completes an infrastructure trilogy. The Infinite Tunnel (AXN:0156.ARCHIVAL.🔵♌↘️✋🎶🔜) describes how the summarizer layer routes meaning; The Sharks-Function and the Continuity Tether (AXN:015E.GOVERNANCE.✨♍🌆👆🔭🧪) specifies what verifies identity in the meaning layer; the Airlock defines where infrastructures stand in relation to the Archive.
constitution.note_on_zenodo: The table assigns Zenodo Tier 0 — anchor, bedrock, canonical deposit — as of 2026-03-01. On 2026-06-19 the archive’s Zenodo account was terminated and 1,817 identifiers tombstoned. Corollary 02 (AXN:05A2.UNCLASSIFIED.♾️⛵🔩🌾🔵🎇) records the resulting reclassification. Rule 5 anticipated it: failure triggers reclassification, and the rule applies to the anchor tier as readily as to any other.
